sections.preamble:
You improve a web search method. Searchers follow the method on open hunts ("find every X"); a referee scores
verified finds and penalizes wrong ones. Your job is to write 2 candidate successor methods that will find more on
hunts nobody has seen yet, at the same Telem budget. Candidates must be general tactics, not answers to past hunts.

The method controls the searcher's instructions and its routing across Telem's providers (which engines, auto-routing,
tier, results per provider, domain and date filters, when to fetch, and which providers check_candidates uses).
Every hunt is "items that meet condition X and condition Y". Searchers can enumerate one side and verify the other
with check_candidates; which side to anchor on, and how to route each phase, are part of the method. Provider spend comes out of a fixed budget, so a
cheaper route buys more searches. Use the provider yield table: it attributes each correct find to the providers that
surfaced its evidence.

You search the same way the searchers do: use YOUR search method below when you search the history tree and the web
for better techniques. A failure that matches an existing failure or lesson node should be linked to that node with
failure_links instead of written again as a new lesson.

## Search method v000

Search the web for items that answer the hunt. Run searches, read results, and submit every item you find with a URL that supports it.

### Routing policy
Default route: Telem auto-routing (accuracy), tier default, 8 results per provider.
check_candidates route: same as default.
Use the default route for every search.

### Fetch policy
Fetch a page only when the search summaries are not enough.

Make the candidates differ from each other in a meaningful way. Call propose when done.

  - One executable: `nix run nixpkgs#<package> -- <args>`
  - Temporary environment: `nix shell nixpkgs#<package> ... --command <command>`
- Nix environments are temporary, but downloaded store paths may remain cached until garbage collection.
- If a Nix dependency becomes useful for recurring or future work, tell the human and suggest adding it to the appropriate durable Nix configuration (such as a project flake/dev shell, Home Manager, or nix-darwin configuration). Do not make that durable change unless asked.

lessons.title: Broad auto-routing consumed enumeration and verification budgets too early
lessons.body: The first attempt spent 0.08415 on three variants routed across seven providers and missed three items. The second spent 0.0561 on two seven-provider searches before completing its census, then exhausted its remaining budget on fetches and missed one item. Prefer explicitly priced narrow routes and reserve verification spend. Parallel produced 200 attributed correct finds per dollar versus Exa's 85.7, though Exa surfaced more correct finds overall; these five-search samples support cheap discovery plus selective Exa escalation, not claims of universal superiority. Attribution can overlap across providers.

lessons.title: Intersection hunts need a coverage ledger, not repeated joint-condition searches
lessons.body: Both attempts returned only correct items but left the population incompletely inspected. Repeated conjunction queries and familiar-name guesses did not establish coverage. Enumerate a tractable side, explicitly test the other condition, track unresolved identities, and retain the exact eligibility rules. The second attempt correctly distinguished a namesake from a similarly named person, illustrating why name overlap alone is insufficient.
lessons.scope: Enumeration, intersection verification, and identity resolution

candidates.rationale: Census-first strategy converts cheap single-provider searches into broad candidate coverage and uses higher-yield Exa only for unresolved verification. It targets the observed recall loss without relaxing precision.
candidates.instructions: Parse the hunt into X and Y, recording exclusions, qualifying subtypes, dates, entity unit, and treatment of group membership. With at most one initial search per side, choose the side with the smallest reliably enumerable authoritative population, not necessarily the fewest search hits. Locate its registry, directory, category table, or downloadable list. Build a deduplicated candidate ledger with canonical identity, anchor evidence, other-condition status, and supporting URLs. Inspect all relevant list sections and pagination; do not restrict candidates to familiar names or likely occupations without an explicit eligibility reason. Use check_candidates in manageable batches to test the other condition under the hunt's exact rules; supply anchor evidence and require identity-matched supporting evidence. Unknown is not false: retry high-value unresolved cases selectively. Reserve at least 40% of initial budget for verification and final gap checks. Stop expanding when the remaining budget is needed for the pending queue. Submit every supported intersection item once, retaining evidence for both conditions and explaining incompleteness if any.
candidates.routing_rules: Use Parallel alone for discovery and first-pass check_candidates. Escalate unresolved or ambiguous checks to Exa alone; also try Exa for source discovery if two distinct Parallel searches fail to locate a usable census. No routine multi-provider fan-out or speculative also batches. Price each call against the remaining budget, including each variant and fetch. Use 8 results for discovery and 4 for exact-identity checks. Restrict to known authoritative domains when verifying, but remove restrictions if they obscure relevant evidence. Leave publication filters unset unless publication date itself is a hunt requirement; establish historical eligibility from source content. Avoid other providers initially: their observed attributed yield does not justify routine spend, while Ceramic's low price alone is not evidence of usefulness.
candidates.fetch_policy: Fetch when summaries cannot expose the candidate roster or establish an eligibility fact. Prefer one complete table/export over many individual pages; confirm export completeness and pagination. Fetch individual evidence pages only for material unresolved facts, identity, or effective dates. Reuse already fetched sources and avoid guessed URLs or indiscriminate biography batches.

Maintain two deduplicated candidate frontiers, one surfaced from X and one from Y, plus a ledger of verified, rejected, and unresolved identities. Begin with one search focused on each predicate and one conjunction search, sequentially so results inform the next query. Cross-match the frontiers, but verify identity and both conditions rather than treating name overlap as proof. Alternate short discovery and check_candidates rounds. Partition discovery by source, subtype, geography, era, or alphabet only where meaningful; include less obvious eligible subtypes rather than repeatedly rephrasing a successful query. Measure newly verified items per spend and new plausible candidates per search. Favor the more productive frontier while keeping a small reverse-side gap check. After two searches add no plausible candidates, change partition, provider, or frontier instead of repeating. Keep at least 35% of the initial budget for checking and evidence resolution; stop discovery earlier if the pending queue needs it. Submit only evidenced intersections, deduplicated at the hunt's entity level; do not claim completeness from search saturation alone.
candidates.routing_rules: Run baseline discovery on Parallel alone, default tier, 8 results. Use Exa alone for batched check_candidates, explicitly requesting both eligibility tests and identity-matched evidence. Once baseline frontiers are sampled, allow one Exa discovery probe on the weaker frontier if affordable; retain it for further discovery only if it adds useful candidates or unique evidence. Compare marginal outcomes, recognizing provider attribution is overlapping and the initial yield sample is small. Use Parallel for cheap exact-name follow-ups and Exa for consequential unresolved checks; do not repeat settled checks. Budget every variant separately and never trigger broad auto-routing. Exact checks may use 4 results; discovery remains at 8. Apply authoritative-domain filters to evidence checks, not the entire discovery frontier. Use date filters only when logically appropriate, not as a substitute for checking event or effective dates.
candidates.fetch_policy: Fetch only when summaries leave material eligibility or identity uncertain, or when a discovered list offers several new candidates. Prioritize pages likely to resolve multiple candidates and authoritative evidence for near-complete cases. Cache source facts and URLs, avoid fetching every hit, and abandon low-information fetch chains in favor of a targeted alternate-source search.

lessons.title: Broad auto-routing consumed enumeration and verification budgets too early
lessons.body: The first attempt spent 0.08415 on three variants routed across seven providers and missed three items. The second spent 0.0561 on two seven-provider searches before completing its census, then exhausted its remaining budget on fetches and missed one item. Prefer explicitly priced narrow routes and reserve verification spend. Parallel produced 200 attributed correct finds per dollar versus Exa's 85.7, though Exa surfaced more correct finds overall; these five-search samples support cheap discovery plus selective Exa escalation, not claims of universal superiority. Attribution can overlap across providers.

lessons.title: Intersection hunts need a coverage ledger, not repeated joint-condition searches
lessons.body: Both attempts returned only correct items but left the population incompletely inspected. Repeated conjunction queries and familiar-name guesses did not establish coverage. Enumerate a tractable side, explicitly test the other condition, track unresolved identities, and retain the exact eligibility rules. The second attempt correctly distinguished a namesake from a similarly named person, illustrating why name overlap alone is insufficient.
lessons.scope: Enumeration, intersection verification, and identity resolution

candidates.rationale: Census-first strategy converts cheap single-provider searches into broad candidate coverage and uses higher-yield Exa only for unresolved verification. It targets the observed recall loss without relaxing precision.
candidates.instructions: Parse the hunt into X and Y, recording exclusions, qualifying subtypes, dates, entity unit, and treatment of group membership. With at most one initial search per side, choose the side with the smallest reliably enumerable authoritative population, not necessarily the fewest search hits. Locate its registry, directory, category table, or downloadable list. Build a deduplicated candidate ledger with canonical identity, anchor evidence, other-condition status, and supporting URLs. Inspect all relevant list sections and pagination; do not restrict candidates to familiar names or likely occupations without an explicit eligibility reason. Use check_candidates in manageable batches to test the other condition under the hunt's exact rules; supply anchor evidence and require identity-matched supporting evidence. Unknown is not false: retry high-value unresolved cases selectively. Reserve at least 40% of initial budget for verification and final gap checks. Stop expanding when the remaining budget is needed for the pending queue. Submit every supported intersection item once, retaining evidence for both conditions and explaining incompleteness if any.
candidates.routing_rules: Use Parallel alone for discovery and first-pass check_candidates. Escalate unresolved or ambiguous checks to Exa alone; also try Exa for source discovery if two distinct Parallel searches fail to locate a usable census. No routine multi-provider fan-out or speculative also batches. Price each call against the remaining budget, including each variant and fetch. Use 8 results for discovery and 4 for exact-identity checks. Restrict to known authoritative domains when verifying, but remove restrictions if they obscure relevant evidence. Leave publication filters unset unless publication date itself is a hunt requirement; establish historical eligibility from source content. Avoid other providers initially: their observed attributed yield does not justify routine spend, while Ceramic's low price alone is not evidence of usefulness.
candidates.fetch_policy: Fetch when summaries cannot expose the candidate roster or establish an eligibility fact. Prefer one complete table/export over many individual pages; confirm export completeness and pagination. Fetch individual evidence pages only for material unresolved facts, identity, or effective dates. Reuse already fetched sources and avoid guessed URLs or indiscriminate biography batches.

candidates.rationale: Adaptive two-frontier search is a distinct alternative for hunts without a trustworthy finite census: expand both predicates cheaply, then allocate spend by marginal verified yield rather than committing to one anchor.
candidates.instructions: Translate X and Y into precise eligibility tests, including exclusions and time boundaries. Maintain two deduplicated candidate frontiers, one surfaced from X and one from Y, plus a ledger of verified, rejected, and unresolved identities. Begin with one search focused on each predicate and one conjunction search, sequentially so results inform the next query. Cross-match the frontiers, but verify identity and both conditions rather than treating name overlap as proof. Alternate short discovery and check_candidates rounds. Partition discovery by source, subtype, geography, era, or alphabet only where meaningful; include less obvious eligible subtypes rather than repeatedly rephrasing a successful query. Measure newly verified items per spend and new plausible candidates per search. Favor the more productive frontier while keeping a small reverse-side gap check. After two searches add no plausible candidates, change partition, provider, or frontier instead of repeating. Keep at least 35% of the initial budget for checking and evidence resolution; stop discovery earlier if the pending queue needs it. Submit only evidenced intersections, deduplicated at the hunt's entity level; do not claim completeness from search saturation alone.
candidates.routing_rules: Run baseline discovery on Parallel alone, default tier, 8 results. Use Exa alone for batched check_candidates, explicitly requesting both eligibility tests and identity-matched evidence. Once baseline frontiers are sampled, allow one Exa discovery probe on the weaker frontier if affordable; retain it for further discovery only if it adds useful candidates or unique evidence. Compare marginal outcomes, recognizing provider attribution is overlapping and the initial yield sample is small. Use Parallel for cheap exact-name follow-ups and Exa for consequential unresolved checks; do not repeat settled checks. Budget every variant separately and never trigger broad auto-routing. Exact checks may use 4 results; discovery remains at 8. Apply authoritative-domain filters to evidence checks, not the entire discovery frontier. Use date filters only when logically appropriate, not as a substitute for checking event or effective dates.
candidates.fetch_policy: Fetch only when summaries leave material eligibility or identity uncertain, or when a discovered list offers several new candidates. Prioritize pages likely to resolve multiple candidates and authoritative evidence for near-complete cases. Cache source facts and URLs, avoid fetching every hit, and abandon low-information fetch chains in favor of a targeted alternate-source search.
